subject: Hosted vs Dedicated — latency/throughput decision follow-up
messages:
From: Sara Lee <sara.lee@finpay.com>

Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: latency/throughput constraints from today's call

Thanks again for the quick demo today — appreciate you walking us through Redwood's routing and batching behavior. A couple of clarifications from our side so we can share with engineering and procurement:

- Primary use case: real-time customer chat (web + mobile) — target p95 end-to-end generation latency <= 250 ms for 1-2 turn interactions. Expected steady concurrent users: ~500 during peak; expected growth to 2,000 within 6 months.
- Secondary use case: batch document embedding generation for search index refresh — approx 200k docs/day, but can be scheduled off-peak. Throughput for embedding job isn't time-sensitive, but cost matters.
- Peak QPS for scoring (short synchronous calls): estimated 3,000 req/s for short prompts (<= 128 tokens), average response size small.

Question: given these requirements, is Hosted API likely to meet the p95 250 ms for chat at 500 concurrent users and up to 3k req/s spikes, or do we need Dedicated capacity from day one? If Dedicated, rough ballpark for monthly committed capacity and a POC path would be helpful. Also looping in Mike (infra) for any security questions.

I've attached our perf_requirements.xlsx with the traffic breakdown.

Thanks,
Sara
Sara Lee
Head of Product, FinPay

Subject: Re: Follow-up: latency/throughput constraints from today's call

Sara — thanks for the summary and the attachment. Quick answers up front, then proposed next steps.

Short answer: Hosted API can handle low-throughput, low-concurrency workloads with predictable p95s, but at the scale and p95 target you're describing (250 ms p95 at sustained multi-hundred concurrent users and 3k spikes) we typically recommend Dedicated for predictable tail latency and throughput.

Why Dedicated likely makes sense here:
- Reserved GPU pools give predictable kernel placement and less noisy neighbors vs multi-tenant hosted instances — that improves tail latency stability.
- Autoscaling/burst policies on Dedicated are configurable to keep p95 within your SLOs during spikes.
- We can offer colocated routing (region) to reduce network hops for your mobile/web clients.

Hosted API notes:
- Typical hosted p95 for short prompts on our curated models is ~80–180 ms in the regions tested, but variance increases with high sustained QPS and long KV cache misses.
- For spikes beyond a few hundred req/s per model, we rely on multi-tenant capacity which can cause transient higher tails.

Suggested POC / next steps:
1) Perf smoke test: we run a short (48–72h) throughput/latency test using a representative prompt set (we'll use your perf_requirements.xlsx). We will instrument p50/p95/p99 and token cost.
2) If the smoke test shows host variability around your target p95, we provision a small Dedicated pool for a week to compare head-to-head.
3) Based on POC, we provide a capacity recommendation + estimated committed monthly price.

I attached a short PDF with an initial estimate for a Dedicated starting configuration (redwood_perf_estimate.pdf) — ballpark only. For procurement, we'll need an internal headcount to sign (legal), and we can start with a month-long trial commitment.

I'll coordinate with Neha on security questions and a HubSpot deal record. Proposed timeline: kick off perf test next Tue (9/21) if that works for your infra team.

Thanks — AD
Aditya Rao
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

- Can you confirm whether Dedicated would allow us to bring our own VPC peering or private link? We need traffic between our app servers and model endpoints to stay in our VPC where possible.
- Any network egress costs we should expect for high-throughput scoring?

If Dedicated gives us private connectivity and full metrics, we are comfortable running a week-long Dedicated trial to validate p95 at scale.

Mike / Sara — great questions. Confirming details so we have a clear mutual action plan.

Answers:
- Private connectivity: yes — Dedicated supports VPC peering and private link options for supported clouds. We'll coordinate networking IP ranges and a short security questionnaire.
- Egress: standard cloud egress applies; for high-throughput scoring we can model estimated egress cost and include it in the final capacity estimate. We'll provide a per-token cost estimate + expected egress.
- Telemetry: for the POC we will expose:
  - Per-route QPS and latency (p50/p95/p99)
  - Pod/instance-level CPU/GPU utilization
  - Token throughput and KV cache hit rate
  - Traces for cold-start/first-token cases
We can publish these via a metrics endpoint and a temporary Grafana dashboard we share with your ops team.

Proposed mutual action plan:
1) Confirm POC dates: dedicated trial provisioned 2027-09-21 to 2027-09-28 (1 week) — running both hosted baseline tests and Dedicated trial side-by-side.
2) We (Redwood) will need: test API keys (we can provide scoped test keys), your representative prompt set (you provided), and network CIDR for VPC peering (if you want private link during trial).
3) Redwood will deliver: perf report (p50/p95/p99), Grafana access, and a recommended committed configuration + pricing within 3 business days after the trial.
4) Next commercial step: 1-month minimum commit for Dedicated, then scale to quarterly/annual after initial validation.
